description: #555: addresses the claim may name as the destination of the own key of a provider of the models.dev catalog (a provider outside the registry), with the verdict each must get. `accepted` is a plain public https address in exactly the spelling the app writes it (lower-case name of at least two labels, no default port, no trailing slash, a plain path of letters, digits and . _ ~ - only). `refused` is anything else: another scheme, a port, credentials, a query, another spelling of an address, a local or private destination, a name that is no public name, an IP address of any kind (a catalog provider has a name; a literal IPv4 or IPv6 address, bracketed, with a zone id, mapped or in a number spelling, is refused so neither side has to agree on which literals are public). The app (`app/src/native-cost/catalog-address.ts`) refuses before it builds an entry; the runner (`dynamic_review/passthrough/destination.py`) refuses again before it uses the key; both are held to this file, so neither side can accept what the other refuses. A name that merely looks public is not judged by either (the connection judges every address a name resolves to). Dummy names only.
